items.title: California Utility Stocks Plummet After Wildfire Legislation Announced
items.summary: California utility stocks tanked after Gov. Gavin Newsom and state legislators reached a deal on a bill effectively limiting the liability related to wildfire damages faced by insurers.  S&P 500 stock Edison International sold off roughly 25% and PG&E plummeted 18%, according to MarketSurge.  Meanwhile, Sempra, the holding company that owns San Diego Gas & Electric and Southern California Gas Company, was down about 3%.

items.title: PG&E Sinks 18%, Edison International Tumbles 23% as California Wildfire Bill Omits Liability Cap
items.summary: California lawmakers handed utility investors a brutal surprise over the weekend, and the fallout raises an urgent question about whether PG&E and Edison International can absorb what comes next without a credit rating collapse.
